The country's transport minister resigned following the crash (is associated with: «Spain's transport minister resigns following deadly train accident») Diego Radamés/EUROPA PRESS/dpaNearly a week after 69 people were killed when a high-speed train slammed into one on the tracks in the Spanish municipality of Urda, Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente resigned on Tuesday.

Transport Minister Óscar Puente made the surprising announcement at the end of his hearing before the parliamentary committee in Madrid. Puente also announced late in the evening that he would not stand in the early parliamentary election on November 29.

The resignation, demanded by all opposition parties, came as a surprise, as Puente and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez had ruled it out several times in recent days.

Puente said: "A minister cannot remain in office after two accidents of this severity within less than a year," Puente said.

"It is a matter of political dignity, consistency and political empathy."
